rationale: Published clinical cohorts of individuals with biallelic GTF3C3 variants (neurodevelopmental disorder with dysmorphic facies, brain anomalies, and seizures; OMIM #621201) confirm that structural anomalies of the corpus callosum (such as hypoplasia or agenesis) are variable and present in only a subset of affected individuals (~40-45%). Brain neuroimaging in reported cohorts reveals variable neuroanatomical involvement—frequently showing cerebellar atrophy and frontal hypoplasia, with corpus callosum hypoplasia or agenesis occurring in less than half of evaluated cases. Consequently, the absence of corpus callosum anomalies does not rule out biallelic pathogenic variants in GTF3C3.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 12 individuals from 7 unrelated families with biallelic GTF3C3 variants, individuals presented with intellectual disability, motor impairments, seizures, and variable cerebellar and corpus callosum malformations, indicating non-obligate penetrance of corpus callosum anomalies.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 result in an autosomal recessive disorder with intellectual disability
source.quote: The cohort presented with intellectual disability, variable nonfamilial facial features, motor impairments, seizures, and cerebellar/corpus callosum malformations.

evidence.text: Evaluation of 4 patients from 3 unrelated families with biallelic GTF3C3 variants demonstrated brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement and frontal lobe hypoplasia, rather than obligate corpus callosum agenesis across all patients.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: Their brain imaging showed brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement, as well as hypoplasia of the frontal lobes and one patient had moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern. Seizures were observed in half of the patients.

evidence.text: Curation and expert panel reviews for GTF3C3 classify the phenotype as neurodevelopmental disorder with hypoplasia of corpus callosum and/or cerebellar atrophy, explicitly highlighting the variable presentation of corpus callosum anomalies.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of corpus callosum dysgenesis compared to cerebellar atrophy across pooled international registries of GTF3C3 patients?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether cerebellar vermis hypoplasia/atrophy is more sensitive or specific than corpus callosum anomalies will improve neuroimaging-directed prioritisation of exome sequencing.

new_directions.question_text: Does the specific functional impact of GTF3C3 missense versus truncating or splice-altering variants correlate with the presence or severity of forebrain commissural defects?
new_directions.rationale: Genotype-phenotype analyses in Drosophila and zebrafish models show variable Pol III transcription impairment; correlating variant severity with commissural axonal guidance phenotypes may reveal why only a subset exhibit callosal malformations.
